title: Functions made by a macro
description:
Write a macro `MAKE_ADDER 2` (a name and a number) that defines a function `add_<name>` returning `rdi` plus the number. Then use it to make `add_ten` (10), `add_hundred` (100) and `add_minus_one` (−1).

| Call | Result |
|---|---|
| `add_ten(5)` | 15 |
| `add_hundred(-100)` | 0 |
| `add_minus_one(0)` | −1 |

starter.solution.asm:
%macro MAKE_ADDER 2
%endmacro

add_ten:
        mov     rax, rdi
        ret

solution.solution.asm:
%macro MAKE_ADDER 2
add_%1:
        lea     rax, [rdi + %2]
        ret
%endmacro

MAKE_ADDER ten, 10
MAKE_ADDER hundred, 100
MAKE_ADDER minus_one, -1

hints: `add_%1:` in the macro body glues the first argument onto `add_`, so `MAKE_ADDER ten, 10` produces a label `add_ten`.
rules: Make add_ten with the macro: MAKE_ADDER ten, 10.
unitTests:
test "adders"
    add_ten(5) == 15
    add_ten(-10) == 0
    add_hundred(-100) == 0
    add_hundred(1) == 101
    add_minus_one(0) == -1

rules.message: Make add_ten with the macro: MAKE_ADDER ten, 10.

grading.unitTests:
test "adders"
    add_ten(5) == 15
    add_ten(-10) == 0
    add_hundred(-100) == 0
    add_hundred(1) == 101
    add_minus_one(0) == -1
